The sound TH

The letters <th> are two sounds, and neither of them exists in French.

The rule

The mouth position: tip of the tongue between the teeth, and blow gently. Not behind the teeth. Between them. You should be able to see it in a mirror.

the quiet th

No vibration. Hand on the throat: nothing.

think, three, thick, Thursday

method, author, something

month, both, earth, depth

the buzzing th

Vibration. Hand on the throat: a buzz.

the, they, this, that, there

other, weather, northern

breathe, bathe, with

Content word → quiet   ·   Grammar word → buzzing
think, three, thick are things. the, this, that, they are glue.

Two more rules, for the middle and the end of a word:

① In the middle: buzzing between two vowels (weather, other, northern). But a Greek or Latin word stays quiet anyway: method, mathematics, cathode, and Ethernet, which sits between two vowels and stays quiet regardless, because the word is Greek.

② At the end: the noun is quiet, the verb buzzes. breath (noun, quiet) but breathe (verb, buzzing). Same for bath and bathe.

The exceptions, where <th> really is a plain t, are: Thailand, Thames, Thomas, Anthony, Theresa, apartheid.

1 · The throat test

  1. Put the flat of your hand on the front of your throat.
  2. Say think. Hold the first sound: thhhhh. Your hand feels nothing. That is the quiet th.
  3. Now say this. Hold it: thhhhh. Your hand feels a buzz. That is the buzzing th.
  4. Go back and forth: think, this, think, this. The tongue does not move. Only the buzz switches on and off.
Same tongue. Same teeth. Same air.
The only difference is whether your throat is switched on.

2 · Zat is ze question

French does not have these sounds, so we borrow the nearest one. The trouble is that the nearest one is a different word. Tap either word to hear it.

Notice that there is no single wrong sound. Depending on the word we reach for s, f, z, d or t. That is why "just say z" does not fix it, and why the tongue has to go between the teeth instead.

3 · Buzz or no buzz?

Hand on the throat. Say the word out loud first, then choose. You will see the reason after each one.

4 · The lab words

Words you will actually say this year. Tap to hear, then say each one with the tongue between the teeth.

earth is the one to get right. In British English the earth wire is the earth wire, and the word ends in the quiet th, tongue between the teeth. Not "eart", not "erf".

5 · Say it

Read aloud, slowly. The underlined letter buzzes. The orange letter is quiet. Then again at speed.

The thermal sensor sends three values through the Ethernet port.
Put the probe beneath this panel, then check the earth.
The north side and the northern side: same root, and the sound changes.
What is the width, the depth and the length of this board?

No buzzthink · three · through · beneath · north · south · earth · month · depth · width · length
Greek, so quiet anywaymethod · mathematics · cathode · Ethernet · thermal · thermistor
Noun quiet, verb buzzingbreath / breathe · bath / bathe · cloth / clothe
Really a plain t (short list)Thailand · Thames · Thomas · Anthony · Theresa · apartheid

A dictionary will write the quiet th as /θ/ and the buzzing th as /ð/. Those two symbols are the only thing on this page you cannot work out with your hand on your throat, and you do not need them here.
